reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In a game, Mysong and Naoki are making problems. They each have four cards like these.

[1] [2] [3] [4]

The winner of the game is the person who can make the problem with the largest answer.

Mysong placed the cards like this.

[Image: Mysong's card placement]

Naoki placed the cards like this.

[Image: Naoki's card placement]

Who won this game? ____
How do you know? ____
____

descriptors: Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 9, which is the difference between 64 and 55) with a correct verbal explanation.
Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 43 − 31 > 24 − 21) with an unsatisfactory explanation.
Mysong. 64 and 55 are shown (or 43 − 31 > 24 − 21) without any further explanation.
Mysong. The response given is a verbal explanation. Either 64 or 55 is shown but not both.
Mysong. The response gives no verbal or numeric explanation.
Other responses containing Mysong. For example, “because Mysong had the largest answer.”
Neither Mysong nor Naoki win.
Naoki. There may or may not be an explanation.
Other incorrect, including “both won.”

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
